tagline: Through Derry to the farm Frost wrote from.
intro: The byway comes south on NH 28 through Derry village and out Rockingham Road to the farm where Robert Frost lived from 1900 to 1911, then wanders east on local roads until it meets the old stage road, NH 121, at Hampstead. Its theme is the country his poems brought to life, the villages and farmsteads and orchards.

Derry was settled by Scots-Irish families in 1719, and the first potato planted in the United States went into their common field that year. Alan Shepard, the first American astronaut in space, was born in Derry, and the town calls itself Spacetown.

moments.title: East Derry
moments.text: The Upper Village, Derry's oldest settlement, keeps its 1769 First Church with the settlers' burying ground behind it, and the house where Alan Shepard grew up.

moments.title: Robert Frost Farm
moments.text: The neighbors thought Frost a lazy farmer, and he later agreed, but most of the poems in his first two books were written in this clapboard farmhouse.
